findings.issue_text: In GoogleCalendar CalendarService.ts updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback when externalCalendarId is falsy is broken because find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) can never match when externalCalendarId is falsy, silently breaking reschedule/cancel for bookings without externalCalendarId

In EventManager.ts (~line 116), destructuring evt.destinationCalendar to undefined when null/empty then dereferencing mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws TypeError for users without a destinationCalendar selecting Google Meet

In organizations create.handler.ts (~line 150), the IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for slug is inverted, causing slug to be omitted for orgs created without team billing enabled, likely breaking org creation/lookup

In office365calendar and larkcalendar CalendarService.ts, COLLECTIVE multi-host events always target destinationCalendar[0] because createEvent signatures lack credentialId parameter, so team members' calendars never get the event and the organizer's calendar may be written multiple times or by wrong credentials

In EventManager.ts (~line 590) catch block in updateCalendarRefs, errors are masked by returning [] instead of a { success: false } entry, silently swallowing errors when calendarReference is undefined

In handleNewBooking.ts (~line 721) loadUsers catch, PrismaClientKnownRequestError is mapped to HTTP 400 with raw Prisma message potentially leaking DB internals, while other errors lose their original message by being converted to generic 500

In EventManager.ts (~line 166), the no-credentialId path yields undefined externalCalendarId in created references because result.externalId is undefined when createEvent is called without externalId, breaking reschedule/cancel for legacy Google Calendar bookings

Logic inversion in organization create slug handling: condition `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` was accidentally inverted to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` in a ternary refactor, flipping which environments get the slug directly vs via the requestedSlug flow

TypeError in EventManager when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/empty/has no entries: code dereferences `.integration` on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` which is undefined, breaking the Meet→Daily fallback for events without a destination calendar

Google Calendar updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is now a no-op: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, `find()` searches for entries whose `externalId` equals a falsy value and returns undefined, causing updates/deletes to silently target the wrong calendar ('primary')

Credentials fetched from DB without ownership verification in createAllCalendarEvents, updateAllCalendarEvents, and handleCancelBooking: `prisma.credential.findUnique` fetches by ID alone with no userId/teamId check, widening IDOR attack surface for calendar credentials

Collective team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none: `evt.destinationCalendar` is null and `?.push(...)` becomes a no-op, discarding all team-member destination calendars for collective events without an organizer destination calendar

Only the first destination calendar is persisted on the booking: `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected while the rest of the array is dropped, causing later flows (cancellation, reschedule, reminders, payment webhooks) to only see the first calendar

Sequential `await createEvent` inside a `for…of` loop in `createAllCalendarEvents` (~line 360) causes N sequential HTTP round-trips for N hosts instead of parallelizing with `Promise.all`, inconsistent with the non-credentialId branch which correctly uses `Promise.all`

N+1 credential DB lookups in per-destination/per-reference loops in `createAllCalendarEvents` (~line 344), `updateAllCalendarEvents` (~line 505), and `handleCancelBooking.ts` (~line 425) issue separate `prisma.credential.findUnique` queries for un-cached credentials instead of batching into a single `prisma.credential.findMany`

Webhook payload `destinationCalendar` changed from object/null to array/null, breaking external consumers that access properties like `externalId` or `integration` directly on it

Organization `create.handler.ts` slug condition inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`, causing organizations to not get a slug when billing is disabled

Null-dereference crash in Google Meet fallback: accessing `.integration` on undefined `mainHostDestinationCalendar` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, crashing booking creation for Google Meet bookings without an explicit destination calendar

Broken fallback in Google Calendar `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent`: self-referential `find` predicate searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals the already-falsy `externalCalendarId`, always returning undefined instead of falling back to the main host's calendar

adjudication_records.issue_text: In GoogleCalendar CalendarService.ts updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback when externalCalendarId is falsy is broken because find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) can never match when externalCalendarId is falsy, silently breaking reschedule/cancel for bookings without externalCalendarId

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, the fallback path when `externalCalendarId` is falsy now does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. If `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, that `find` predicate can’t match any normal destination calendar (which will have a real `externalId`), so the computed calendar id becomes `undefined`. That means updates/deletes will either be sent with an undefined calendarId (error) or fall back to some default elsewhere (e.g., `primary`), which is incorrect for bookings that don’t have `externalCalendarId` on the reference. This regression is directly visible in the diff: the prior fallback used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single object), but the new array-based fallback is implemented incorrectly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google Calendar updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is now a no-op: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, `find()` searches for entries whose `externalId` equals a falsy value and returns undefined, causing updates/deletes to silently target the wrong calendar ('primary')

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar id like:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

and similarly for `calendarId` in `deleteEvent`.

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the exact condition that triggers the fallback), the `find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so it will almost always return `undefined` rather than a real destination calendar. This makes the fallback effectively broken compared to the previous behavior (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` when it was a single object).

Additionally, `deleteEvent` defines `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, implying it will proceed with `primary` when the computed `calendarId` is undefined, so updates/deletes can silently apply to the wrong calendar instead of the intended destination calendar(s).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credentials fetched from DB without ownership verification in createAllCalendarEvents, updateAllCalendarEvents, and handleCancelBooking: `prisma.credential.findUnique` fetches by ID alone with no userId/teamId check, widening IDOR attack surface for calendar credentials

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new fallback paths that load credentials directly from the database using only the numeric credential ID, e.g. in `createAllCalendarEvents` (lookup by `destination.credentialId`), `updateAllCalendarEvents` (lookup by `reference.credentialId`), and `handleCancelBooking` (lookup by `credentialId`). In all cases the query is `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: ... } })` (or equivalent) and the returned credential is then used to perform calendar operations. There is no verification that the fetched credential belongs to the current booking/user/team (no `userId`/`teamId` constraint), so if an attacker can influence the stored `credentialId` values (e.g., via booking/destinationCalendar/reference data), this widens an IDOR-style risk. The lack of ownership verification is directly observable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Collective team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none: `evt.destinationCalendar` is null and `?.push(...)` becomes a no-op, discarding all team-member destination calendars for collective events without an organizer destination calendar

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding refers to code where `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` and `?.push(...)` becomes a no-op, causing team-member destination calendars to be dropped. In the provided diff, there is no `?.push(...)` usage on `destinationCalendar` (or anywhere in the shown hunks). Instead, the changes explicitly construct `destinationCalendar` as an array (e.g., `selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`) and update downstream consumers to treat it as an array. Since the alleged `?.push(...)` logic is not present in this diff, the finding is not a verifiable problem introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only the first destination calendar is persisted on the booking: `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected while the rest of the array is dropped, causing later flows (cancellation, reschedule, reminders, payment webhooks) to only see the first calendar

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and updates multiple call sites to either wrap a single destination in an array or explicitly take only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...`). However, there is no code in this diff that “persists on the booking” by connecting `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` (or any similar Prisma connect) while dropping the rest—no such line exists here. The finding asserts a specific persistence bug across later flows, but the diff only shows event creation/update/delete logic and some places intentionally using the first element; it does not show booking persistence logic that drops additional calendars. Therefore the claimed issue is not directly verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sequential `await createEvent` inside a `for…of` loop in `createAllCalendarEvents` (~line 360) causes N sequential HTTP round-trips for N hosts instead of parallelizing with `Promise.all`, inconsistent with the non-credentialId branch which correctly uses `Promise.all`

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new logic iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and (in the `destination.credentialId` path) performs `const createdEvent = await createEvent(...)` inside the loop, which necessarily runs each calendar creation sequentially. This is directly visible in the diff and contrasts with the other branch that batches calls via `Promise.all(...)`. With multiple destination calendars this introduces avoidable N-round-trip latency (and potential timeout risk) compared to parallelizing the independent HTTP calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 credential DB lookups in per-destination/per-reference loops in `createAllCalendarEvents` (~line 344), `updateAllCalendarEvents` (~line 505), and `handleCancelBooking.ts` (~line 425) issue separate `prisma.credential.findUnique` queries for un-cached credentials instead of batching into a single `prisma.credential.findMany`

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. The diff introduces per-item DB lookups inside loops:
- `createAllCalendarEvents`: iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and when not found in `this.calendarCredentials` performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` per destination.
- `updateAllCalendarEvents`: now processes `calendarReference` as an array and loops `for (const reference of calendarReference)`, doing `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } })` when not found in `this.calendarCredentials`.
- `handleCancelBooking.ts`: loops over `bookingCalendarReference` and for missing `calendarCredential` does `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` per reference.
This is a verifiable N+1 query pattern (potential performance defect) that could be batched via a single `findMany` for all needed IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recurring-event delete logic in `handleCancelBooking.ts` (~line 445) is inside a per-reference loop but iterates over all credentials and bookings independently of the outer reference, causing the same `deleteEvent` API calls to be executed R times (R calendar references), wasting external API quota and generating errors on already-deleted events

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `bookingCalendarReference` was changed from `.find(...)` to `.filter(...)`, and the recurring-event deletion block now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. However, that recurring deletion block builds `promises` by iterating over **all** of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(type.endsWith("_calendar"))` and then over `updatedBookings`, calling `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` for each booking reference found. This inner work does not depend on the outer `reference` (other than being gated by `if (credentialId)`), so if there are R calendar references with `credentialId`, the same set of delete calls will be executed R times, leading to redundant API calls and likely errors for already-deleted events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook payload `destinationCalendar` changed from object/null to array/null, breaking external consumers that access properties like `externalId` or `integration` directly on it

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` from a single object/null to an array form in multiple places (e.g., `CalendarEventClass` type becomes `DestinationCalendar[] | null`, booking reminder now sets `destinationCalendar: selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`). The Playwright webhook e2e expectation is also updated from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, which indicates the webhook payload shape has changed. Any external consumer expecting `destinationCalendar.externalId` / `.integration` directly would break because those properties now live on an array element (e.g., `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google Calendar `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` calendar ID lookup never matches when `externalCalendarId` is falsy because `find()` searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals a falsy value

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the calendarId fallback like:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
(and similarly for `calendarId` in `deleteEvent`).

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g., `undefined`/`null`), the `find()` predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined` (or `=== null`), which will almost never match a real calendar externalId. So the fallback resolves to `undefined` rather than selecting a destination calendar, meaning the calendar ID lookup effectively fails in the falsy `externalCalendarId` case. This is exactly what the finding claims.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only touches calendar-related services and event/booking handling files (e.g., CalendarService.ts, CalendarManager.ts, EventManager.ts, bookingReminder.ts). There is no change to any `create.handler.ts` file, no organization slug logic, and no `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition shown. Therefore the proposed finding cannot be verified from (and is not present in) this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Calendar.createEvent` public interface signature changed to require a `credentialId` parameter without migration, breaking external callers and app-store implementations not updated in this PR
Collective events without organizer destination calendar silently lose team member calendars because `evt.destinationCalendar` is null and `?.push()` is skipped

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` from a single object/null to an array and, in multiple places, explicitly sets it to `[]` when absent (e.g., `bookingReminder.ts`: `selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`, and `handleCancelBooking.ts`: always `[]`/`[dc]`). There is no `?.push()` usage shown in the diff, and the new `createAllCalendarEvents` logic iterates `event.destinationCalendar` when non-empty, otherwise falls back to creating events without destination calendars. So the claim that `evt.destinationCalendar` is null and calendars are silently lost due to a skipped `?.push()` is not verifiable from this diff and appears to be a misreading/speculation about code not present here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only the first destination calendar is persisted to the booking record, so subsequent reschedule/cancel operations for collective events with multiple hosts may not update/delete other hosts' calendars correctly

adjudication.rationale: The diff primarily changes `destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array and updates event creation/update/cancel flows to iterate over multiple destination calendars and multiple `_calendar` references (e.g., `createAllCalendarEvents` loops destinations; `updateCalendarEvent` and `handleCancelBooking` now `filter` and process all calendar references). Nothing in the shown diff demonstrates that only the first destination calendar is persisted to the booking record; persistence of booking records/references is not shown here. In fact, the changes move toward supporting multiple calendars rather than dropping all but the first.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Null-dereference crash in Google Meet fallback: accessing `.integration` on undefined `mainHostDestinationCalendar` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, crashing booking creation for Google Meet bookings without an explicit destination calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the Google Meet fallback was changed from a safe optional-chain check (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) to destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally accessing `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` will throw at runtime if `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. The diff also updates the type to `DestinationCalendar[] | null`, so this case is plausible and the new code introduces a null/undefined dereference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken fallback in Google Calendar `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent`: self-referential `find` predicate searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals the already-falsy `externalCalendarId`, always returning undefined instead of falling back to the main host's calendar
matched_golden_ids: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same logic bug: when `externalCalendarId` is provided, the code uses a `find` predicate comparing `calendar.externalId` to `externalCalendarId` in a way that’s self-referential/tautological and causes the lookup to fail (returning undefined) rather than selecting the correct calendar (e.g., by credentialId or other criteria).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `updateEvent` called with `undefined` credential in `updateAllCalendarEvents`: missing guard when credential isn't in memory and DB lookup returns null or lacks `app.slug`, causing `Promise.all` rejection that fails all calendar updates for the booking
matched_golden_ids: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point to the same core bug: when a reference has a credentialId but the credential cannot be found (in memory or via DB lookup), `updateEvent`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` may be invoked with an undefined/null credential. The candidate additionally notes downstream effects (Promise.all rejection), but it still identifies the same missing guard/handling for absent credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team destination calendars silently dropped for collective events: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` is a no-op when `destinationCalendar` is null, discarding all team member calendars

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references code using `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` and a scenario where `destinationCalendar` is null so the push becomes a no-op. In the provided diff, there is no occurrence of `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` (or any `.push` on `destinationCalendar`) and no shown logic for collective events that appends team member calendars this way. The diff instead changes `destinationCalendar` to be an array and updates callers to set it as `[]` or `[selectedDestinationCalendar]`. Therefore, the claimed issue is not verifiably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Office 365 and Lark `createEvent` always target `destinationCalendar[0]` regardless of which credential is being used, causing collective events with multiple hosts to create duplicates on the organizer's calendar and miss the second host's calendar

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over each destination to create events for multiple calendars/credentials. GoogleCalendarService was updated to select the destination calendar matching the `credentialId`, but Lark and Office365 `createEvent` were changed to always destructure/use only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and then derive `calendarId/eventsUrl` from that. Since `CalendarManager.createEvent` always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`, Lark/Office365 ignore which credential/destination is being processed and will target `destinationCalendar[0]` for every create, which can create duplicates on the first host’s calendar and fail to create on other hosts’ calendars when multiple destinations are present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB-fetched credential in `handleCancelBooking` missing `app` relation include, leaving `appName` absent and potentially causing `getCalendar` to fail to resolve the calendar service for cancellations
Logic regression in updateEvent/deleteEvent: when externalCalendarId is falsy, the find() never matches a real calendar, silently falling back to primary instead of the intended destination calendar

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback logic when externalCalendarId is falsy is incorrect: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares each `cal.externalId` to `externalCalendarId` (which is null/undefined in the fallback branch), so it will almost always return undefined. That makes the effective calendarId undefined and later falls back to "primary" (or otherwise not the intended destination calendar). Previously it used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly (single object), so this is a real regression introduced by the array migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted boolean logic in create.handler.ts: slug is now set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true instead of when it is false, causing a behavioral inversion

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not include any changes to a `create.handler.ts` file, nor does it reference `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` or any logic related to setting a `slug`. All shown changes are in calendar/event management and destinationCalendar handling. Therefore the proposed finding is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent no-op for collective team calendars: when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null and optional chaining ?.push() silently drops team members' calendars

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and, in the touched call sites, explicitly sets it to an empty array when no calendar is selected (e.g. `selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []` in `bookingReminder.ts`, and similar in `handleCancelBooking.ts`). There is no `?.push()` on `evt.destinationCalendar` anywhere in the provided diff, and the described scenario (null + optional chaining push silently dropping calendars) is not verifiable from these changes. While `destinationCalendar`’s type allows `null`, the diff generally moves away from `null` toward `[]` in affected code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Massive duplication of destinationCalendar array-wrapping ternary pattern across 8+ call sites in bookingReminder.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts, handleNewBooking.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, webhook.ts, confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, requestReschedule.handler.ts, and deleteCredential.handler.ts

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show some repeated array-wrapping logic for `destinationCalendar` (e.g., in `bookingReminder.ts` and `handleCancelBooking.ts`). However, the proposed finding claims duplication across 8+ additional call sites/files (handleNewBooking.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, webhook.ts, confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, requestReschedule.handler.ts, deleteCredential.handler.ts) that are not present in the provided diff, so it is not verifiable here. Also, even where repetition exists, it is a maintainability/refactor suggestion rather than a clear bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated credential-from-DB fetching logic (~20 lines) between createAllCalendarEvents and updateCalendarEvent methods in EventManager.ts should be extracted to a shared helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce very similar “fetch credential from DB if not in this.calendarCredentials” blocks in both `createAllCalendarEvents` and `updateCalendarEvent` (each building a `credential` object from `prisma.credential.findUnique`). However, this is a maintainability/refactoring suggestion (DRY) rather than a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change. The code will still function with duplication, so it doesn’t meet the bar for a REAL problem per the instructions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Type boundary leak: adding schedulingType to CalendarEvent leaks an EventType-level concern into the calendar-event domain model, increasing coupling between bookings feature and calendar integrations

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not add or reference `schedulingType` anywhere, nor does it introduce an EventType-level field into `CalendarEvent`. The changes shown are primarily about changing `destinationCalendar` from a single object/null to an array and updating integrations/services accordingly. Therefore the proposed coupling/type-boundary leak claim is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lark and Office365 createEvent implementations ignore the new credentialId parameter, always using destinationCalendar[0] instead of selecting the correct calendar by credential, breaking multi-host collective events

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array (`DestinationCalendar[] | null`) and updates GoogleCalendar `createEvent` to accept `credentialId` and select the matching destination calendar via `find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. However, Lark and Office365 `createEvent` still destructure only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and use that calendar’s `externalId`, with no selection by credential. Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination, but it passes the same `event` object each time (does not narrow `destinationCalendar` to the current destination). This means for destinations beyond index 0, Lark/Office365 will still use `destinationCalendar[0]`, causing events to be created in the wrong calendar and breaking multi-destination/multi-host cases. Also, `CalendarManager.createEvent` now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` for all calendars; Lark/Office365 do not use that parameter to choose the destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed console.error logging from catch block in updateCalendarEvent, causing calendar update failures to be silently swallowed with no server-side log, reducing observability

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` within the `updateCalendarEvent` try/catch, the catch block previously did `console.error(message);` and then returned a failure `EventResult`. The diff removes the `console.error(message);` line and does not replace it with any other logging call in that catch block, so failures handled there will no longer emit a server-side log from this path (even though the function still returns failure results). This reduces observability as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Side-effect inside map callback: teamDestinationCalendars.push() mutates an external array inside the teamMemberPromises map function, mixing data transformation with state mutation

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references `teamDestinationCalendars.push()` being called inside a `teamMemberPromises.map(...)` callback. In the provided diff, there is no occurrence of `teamDestinationCalendars`, no `.push()` on such an array, and no `teamMemberPromises` map callback shown. Since the claimed pattern is not present in the diff, the issue is not verifiable from these changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google `updateEvent` fallback is broken: when `externalCalendarId` is null/undefined, the `find` callback searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals null/undefined, which never matches, causing `selectedCalendar` to be undefined with no 'primary' fallback (unlike `createEvent`), silently failing Google updates for legacy data or null `externalCalendarId` callers

Google `deleteEvent` fallback is broken: same regression as `updateEvent` but on the delete path — with falsy `externalCalendarId`, `calendarId` becomes undefined, causing Google delete to 400 or no-op, resulting in cancelled bookings whose Google events are never removed (silent data retention / privacy issue)

COLLECTIVE team members' calendars are silently dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar: if neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (not `[]`), so the `?.push` is a no-op and all team hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding hinges on `evt.destinationCalendar` becoming `null` and then code doing `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` (a no-op) causing team hosts’ destination calendars to be dropped. In the provided diff, there is no `?.push` (or any push) on `destinationCalendar` shown, so the core mechanism described is not verifiable from this change. Additionally, multiple call sites in the diff explicitly normalize missing destination calendars to an empty array (e.g., `selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []` in `bookingReminder.ts`, and a `... : []` fallback in `handleCancelBooking.ts`), which contradicts the claim that it becomes `null` in these updated paths. While `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is typed as `DestinationCalendar[] | null`, the diff does not demonstrate the specific null+push scenario or silent dropping behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking persistence stores only the first destinationCalendar: for COLLECTIVE events, only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the booking, so subsequent cancel/reschedule/reminder flows only see the organizer's DC, losing multi-host support across later operations

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `destinationCalendar` to an array and several call sites explicitly take only the first element (e.g., Meet fallback in `EventManager`, and in calendar service implementations). However, the proposed finding claims a *persistence* bug (“only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the booking” and later flows therefore lose multi-host DCs). That persistence/linking logic is not shown in this diff, and the diff actually adds multi-destination handling in later operations: `createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and `updateCalendarEvents`/cancel flows are updated to handle multiple `_calendar` references via `.filter(...)` + loops. So the claim that only the first destination calendar is persisted (and thus later flows only see the organizer DC) is not directly verifiable from the provided changes and appears to be a misattribution/speculation beyond the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent credential hydration in `handleCancelBooking` DB fallback: the raw Prisma credential is passed directly to `getCalendar()` without including `app.slug`, unlike the parallel fallback in `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents`, potentially causing the delete path to throw or pick the wrong adapter

Merge path still deletes only the first old calendar reference: the 'delete the old calendar event' step uses `.find` instead of `.filter`, so with multiple `_calendar` references now possible, all but the first are orphaned on reschedule-with-merge, leaving old events on second/third hosts' calendars

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager, calendar references were updated to support multiple `_calendar` references (e.g., `calendarReference` is now an array via `.filter(...)` and processed in a loop). However, in the merge/reschedule path, the cleanup step still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` to get `oldCalendarEvent`, which will only return the first matching calendar reference. With multiple calendar references now possible, this code will delete at most one old calendar event and can leave the remaining old events orphaned on other calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-Google calendar services ignore `credentialId` and only use `mainHostDestinationCalendar[0]`: only `GoogleCalendarService` uses `credentialId` to pick the matching destination calendar, while Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService paths only operate on element 0, silently ignoring team members' calendars for COLLECTIVE events on non-Google adapters

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array and updates `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` to iterate over all destinations and call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each. However, non-Google adapters shown (Lark and Office365) still derive `calendarId` from only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`). They do not select the destination calendar matching the current credential/destination being processed, unlike `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` which explicitly finds the matching calendar by `credentialId`. Because `EventManager` passes the full `event` (with the whole destinationCalendar array) on each iteration, Lark/Office365 will repeatedly use element 0 and ignore other destinations, which is a correctness bug for multi-destination (e.g., collective/team) events on those adapters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `organization` select silently dropped from `loadUsers` query: the previous explicit `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` was removed, so downstream code reading `user.organization.slug` will see `undefined` if `userSelect.select` doesn't already include it

adjudication.rationale: The provided diff does not show any `loadUsers` query, any Prisma `select` changes involving `organization`, or any downstream usage of `user.organization.slug`. All shown changes are around `destinationCalendar` becoming an array and related calendar integrations. Since the claimed removal of `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` is not present in the diff, the finding is not verifiable from this change set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `requestRescheduleHandler` dropped the user fallback to `booking.user.destinationCalendar` entirely: reschedule flows for bookings without a booking-level `destinationCalendar` now pass `[]`, which can cause downstream services (e.g. Lark) to throw 'no calendar id' or fall back to 'primary'

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any `requestRescheduleHandler` changes, so the claim about that handler “dropping the user fallback” is not verifiable from this patch. Where `destinationCalendar` fallback logic *is* shown (e.g., `apps/web/pages/api/cron/bookingReminder.ts` and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`), the code explicitly keeps the fallback to `user.destinationCalendar` / `bookingToDelete.user.destinationCalendar` and only wraps the selected value into an array (otherwise `[]`). Therefore the proposed finding misreads or references code not present in the diff.
